scope: Proposition 11.1 (Deficit inside a fixed small ball) of the manuscript “Uniform excess charge for Coulomb molecules and the outer radius of neutral atoms” (preprints/Uniform-excess-charge-for-Coulomb-molecules-and-the-outer-radius-of-neutral-atoms-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 263 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5abedb3de1f8ed28), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 67. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a universal constant cdef > 0 with the following property. For every D0 ∈ [0, ∞) there is s∗(D0) > 0 such that, for each 0 < s ≤ s∗(D0), there is an integer Z∗(D0, s) for which every integer Z ≥ Z∗(D0, s) and every normalized sector ground state Ψ satisfying n ≤ 3Z, qn[Ψ] = En ≤ E + D0 obey Z − EΨ#{i : |xi| < s/4} ≥ cdefs−3 > 1. (11.1) All thresholds are independent of the sector and of the choice of its ground state. In particular, admissible fixed radii s can be taken arbitrarily small.
